bib.title: Latent Retrieval for Weakly Supervised Open Domain Question Answering
bib.venue: Proceedings of the 57th Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics (ACL 2019), pages 6086-6096

question: Can a retriever and reader be learned jointly from question-answer string pairs alone, without a blackbox IR system or gold evidence?
hypothesis: Pre-training the retriever with an unsupervised Inverse Cloze Task gives a strong enough initialization for end-to-end latent retrieval learning, and learned retrieval beats BM25 when questions reflect a genuine information need.
contributions: ORQA, the first open-retrieval QA system with retriever and reader jointly learned from question-answer pairs without any IR system
Inverse Cloze Task for unsupervised retriever pre-training
Evaluation on five open QA datasets showing learned retrieval matters when question writers do not know the answer

method.summary: ORQA scores answer derivations (block, span) as dense inner-product retrieval score plus a BERT span-reader score. The retriever (two BERT-base encoders projected to 128 dims) is pre-trained with ICT, block encodings are pre-computed, and only the question encoder and reader are fine-tuned on QA pairs by marginal log-likelihood over top-k retrieved blocks.

datasets.name: English Wikipedia 2018-12-20
datasets.size: just over 13 million evidence blocks of at most 288 wordpieces
datasets.preprocessing: greedily split at sentence boundaries; document title included in block encoder

datasets.name: Natural Questions (open)
datasets.preprocessing: only questions with short answers kept, evidence discarded, answers over 5 tokens dropped

models.name: ORQA
models.architecture: two BERT-base bi-encoders (question, block) with 128-dim projections plus BERT-base span reader with MLP over concatenated endpoints

models.name: BM25 + BERT
models.architecture: Lucene BM25 retrieval (title included) with same BERT reader; final score learned weighted sum of BM25 and reader score

models.name: NNLM + BERT
models.architecture: 128-dim context-independent feed-forward LM embeddings, question encoding fine-tuned

models.name: ELMO (small) + BERT
models.architecture: 128-dim bidirectional LSTM embeddings, question encoding fine-tuned

training.objective: ICT pre-training: softmax over in-batch blocks with pseudo-question sentence; fine-tuning: L = L_early (c=5000 blocks, retrieval score only) + L_full (marginal log-likelihood over top k=5 blocks and matching spans)
training.epochs: fine-tuning 2 epochs (NQ, TriviaQA, SQuAD), 20 epochs (WebQuestions, CuratedTrec)
training.regularisation: sentence removed from its context in 90% of ICT examples
training.hardware: ICT on Google Cloud TPUs; fine-tuning on a single machine with a 12GB GPU

other.frozen: all parameters fine-tuned except the evidence block encoder
other.discarded_examples: examples with no matching answer in beam discarded (<10%)
other.dev_split: 10% of train held out for dev when no dev set; when test hidden, original dev used as test

inference.decoding: argmax over (block, span) of S_retr + S_read
inference.samples: single run per dataset; no seeds or variance reported
inference.retrieval: top-k=5 blocks by maximum inner product over pre-computed block encodings (Locality Sensitive Hashing mentioned as an example tool); answer spans limited to 10 tokens

metrics.name: Exact match
metrics.definition: exact match with any reference answer string after minor normalization such as lowercasing, following DrQA scripts

eval.protocol: Dev and test EM per dataset; single reported numbers, no significance test

availability.data: Wikipedia snapshot URL given; no code or weights link stated

evidence.quote: we use a learning rate of 10−4 and a batch size of 4096

limits: 128-dim dense vectors cannot match BM25 on exact word detail; authors say a hybrid approach would be promising future work (Sec 9.3)
SQuAD is unsuitable for learned retrieval: 100k questions from 536 documents violate IID; authors urge not to use it for end-to-end open QA
Single run, no seeds or variance; no code or weights stated
Fine-tuning keeps the block encoder fixed, so retrieval expressivity comes only from the question encoder
Uses 2018 BERT-base; later dense retrievers (DPR etc.) are not compared

terms.definition: given a sentence, predict its context; a sentence is a pseudo-question and its context pseudo-evidence, selected from in-batch candidates
evidence is learned and retrieved from the open corpus, supervised only by question-answer strings
